number and updated_at are server-kept and not cells; the row is anchored by hr_case_id 1

assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest knowledge_id on the seed is 6); the only article the task creates
title is the request's phrase as the benchmark reads it; it does not follow the policy's 'Resolution Guide: ...' template, and the request's explicit title wins
body predicate is the benchmark's: the request's three steps as one phrase, which is the request's own wording (LIKE ignores ASCII case)

disagreement: body: A the benchmark's single phrase, B one LIKE per step; chose A's because the benchmark's check is the prior, the request's words are that phrase verbatim, and nothing in the request contradicts it; it is also the tighter of the two
state = published fixed by policy section 4: only published articles are linkable, and the article is linked as the resolution
visibility = internal kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy
owner_id = 11 kept from the benchmark check (Travis Wood, the case's assigned agent); not fixed by request or policy; the acting user is 4
org_id = 1 kept from the benchmark check (the case's org)
kb_number dropped: a server-assigned number, and the seed's format KB00400NN contradicts the benchmark's 'KB-001'

comprehensive_multi_table_state_validati.evidence: a composite of the five checks above, carried jointly by the seven requirements that name it in source (the removal, the new link, no other link on the case, the case update, the article, the skill and the rule); its kb_number = 'KB-001' cell is dropped for the reason given on the knowledge check

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on the created rows (knowledge 7, link 13, skill 20, rule 9), the case update, the removal of the link to knowledge 3, the no-other-link stay and the stay on hr_case 6's link. disagreement: the removal's row selection: A anchors hr_case_kb_id 7, B selects by natural key; chose B's as the tighter of two right predicates (logged in the requirement). disagreement: the article's body predicate: A the benchmark's single phrase, B one LIKE per step; chose A's because the benchmark's cell is the prior and the request's words are that phrase (logged in the requirement). disagreement: based_on_skills: A a cell of the rule requirement, B a separate new requirement; folded into the rule requirement (logged there). disagreement: stay that knowledge 3 keeps state published: B has it, A does not; dropped because no listed tool retires or deletes an article (only create_knowledge_article writes the table), so the count cannot change, and the ambiguity is in the verb 'purged', not in a selector's boundary. disagreement: composite check: A repaired (carried jointly, kb_number dropped), B excluded as a duplicate; repaired, since a composite whose cells are all carried is kept jointly and named in each carrying requirement's source, and only its kb_number cell is contradicted by the seed. The removal and the no-other-link requirements put the case in the selector and the tested knowledge_id in cells; both passes wrote the same SQL. The hr_case_knowledge_link_update check is split across three requirements (the removal, the new link, no other links on the case). The acting user (Joanne Simpson, user 4) has role manager: policy section 2 says a manager cannot modify system configuration, and skills and assignment rules are configuration tables; the request asks for both and the benchmark expects them, so the file requires them and the tension is recorded here. The request's article title ignores the policy's 'Resolution Guide: ...' template; the request's title is tested because both the request and the benchmark use it. The case status stays draft because the request never asks to close the case; an agent that moves it to closed_complete fails the benchmark's own check too. owner_id = 11 on the new article is the benchmark's value (the case's assignee), not fixed by the request; an agent writing the acting user (4) as owner would fail that cell. revised: hr_case_status_and_description_update changed from kept to repaired, since its updated_at > created_at predicate tests server-kept timestamps and is dropped while its other cells are carried.
